rows.evidence: Q1: Introduction and Main Findings - the brief reports a pilot demonstration activity in the Lower Bari Doab Canal (756,000 ha) in which the authors processed Landsat/Sentinel imagery with SEBAL for 2017-2018, computed 15 irrigation performance indicators per distributary and rotation cycle, calculated Gini coefficients of water delivered, and produced a water deficit table by division (Table 2) and a prototype DSS.
rows.notes: Although a policy brief, it reports the authors' own analysis from the ADB technical assistance study, so Q1 is yes. For Q2 the study does not show that remote sensing improved equity in canal water delivery: it diagnoses existing inequity (Gini coefficients, canal water per unit area differing between divisions and seasons), computes water deficits, and designs a DSS that 'may' guide reallocation; the DSS remained a prototype the PID 'decided to continue developing' and no change in delivery equity was implemented or measured. This is a precondition (diagnostic/monitoring capability) of the claimed effect, so upstream is set. The satellite-derived ET and soil moisture were also not ground validated (Key Points list ground validation as a limitation), so the model output was never checked against field measurements. The brief does state limitations (one year of data, no ground validation), but Q8 is answered no because Q2 is no.

notes: Text is a short ADB brief summarising a larger technical assistance report; figures 1-5 are not rendered in the text, only captions. The brief is complete (8 pages).
